issue.title: Status of testing Providers that were prepared on March 10, 2026
issue.body:
### Body

I have a kind request for all the contributors to the latest provider distributions release.
Could you please help us to test the RC versions of the providers?

The guidelines on how to test providers can be found in

[Verify providers by contributors](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors)

Let us know in the comments, whether the issue is addressed.

These are providers that require testing as there were some substantial changes introduced:

comments.body:
Did a test round with FabAuthManager, EdgeExecutor and Integration Test Dag in Airflow 3.0.6, 3.1.8rc2 and main and all looks good!
(And need to realize that the UI dramatically improved from 3.0.6 to current main! Wow!)
Tested `mongo==5.3.3rc1`, `postgres==6.6.1rc1`, `salesforce==5.12.3rc1`. Connection UI metadata renders correctly for all three (#62444, #62445, #62446). LGTM.
Tested my changes to edge3. All looks good
#62347 works as expected, thanks

#62431 — Verified with `apache-airflow-providers-fab==3.5.0rc1` installed via breeze (FabAuthManager, postgres backend). 
Sequential and concurrent FAB route requests (token generation, users, roles) all return 200/201. No race conditions (KeyError/AttributeError) observed.

Tested #63110 in `apache-airflow-providers-celery==3.17.1rc1` — `execute_workload` (and `execute_command` for Airflow 2.x) are correctly registered with the Celery app at worker startup. The `KeyError: 'execute_command'` / `KeyError: 'execute_workload'` issue from #63043 is resolved.

tested [apache.kafka: 1.13.0rc1](https://pypi.org/project/apache-airflow-providers-apache-kafka/1.13.0rc1), feature added in #62916 works as expected. But found minor issue in docstrings, will fix it in several hours

upd: PR with docstring fix: #63333
#62289 works as expected, Thanks
I tested all my changes and they look good to me

Hey, while testing provider-fab: 3.5.0rc1, I noticed that the specific “Add Permission to Role Error” issue in #62737 is now resolved.
However, the same race condition still appears to be causing failures in three other places that run synchronously during startup.

I'll work on addressing those as well and will try to open a PR today.

Regarding Provider [oracle: 4.5.1rc1] (https://pypi.org/project/apache-airflow-providers-oracle/4.5.1rc1) tested over airflow v3.1.6 does not solve the issue #62526. 
Kind regards.

> Hey, while testing provider-fab: 3.5.0rc1, I noticed that the specific “Add Permission to Role Error” issue in [#62737](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/62737) is now resolved. However, the same race condition still appears to be causing failures in three other places that run synchronously during startup.
> 
> I'll work on addressing those as well and will try to open a PR today.

Are you saying this is a regression? Or some issues are left unresolved? If this is a regression we should not release FAB provider then
Confirmed my changes to `apache-airflow-providers-snowflake` on Airflow 2.11 re: #62378 and #62365

Tested #62604 with the following DAG code and test scenarios, and looks good. 1. ✔️ Set `requirements=["pendulum"]` 2. ✔️ Set `requirements=["pendulum>=3"]` 3. ✔️ Set `requirements=["pendulum<3"]` 4. ❌ Set `requirements=None` 5. ❌ Set `requirements=[""]` The `generate_message` imports `pendulum` and it requires `pendulum` to be specified in the `requirements`. If the `pendulum` is not specified, it will raise an import error. ### DAG code ```python from datetime import datetime, timedelta import pendulum from airflow import DAG from airflow.providers.standard.operators.python import PythonOperator, PythonVirtualenvOperator # Define the DAG with DAG(dag_id="example_virtualenv_dag", start_date=datetime(2025, 5, 1), schedule=None, catchup=False) as dag: # A simple Python callable to be run in the virtualenv def generate_message(*args, **kwargs): import pendulum return f"Hello from virtualenv! pendulum version {pendulum.__version__}" # Task: runs `generate_message` inside a fresh virtual environment virtualenv_task = PythonVirtualenvOperator( task_id="virtualenv_task", python_version="3.9", python_callable=generate_message, requirements=[ "pendulum" ], system_site_packages=False, expect_airflow=False, serializer="dill", ) if __name__ == "__main__": dag_run = dag.test( logical_date=pendulum.datetime(2025, 5, 3) ) # Runs all tasks locally without a scheduler :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2} print("STATE: ", dag_run.state) ```

> Are you saying this is a regression? Or some issues are left unresolved? If this is a regression we should not release FAB provider then

No, this is not a regression. The previous behavior hasn't gotten worse.

What happened is that my previous PR (#62737) successfully fixed the race condition in one specific place (the Add Permission to Role Error). However, that exact same race condition pattern exists in a few other places in the code during startup.
